message.content:
Build bundled EMAIL PROVISIONING for shared hosting in worktree /opt/nxeon-wt-email (branch feature/hosting-email, based on the just-promoted batch). This is the cross-tenant-takeover-sensitive area — the guiding rule is REUSE THE ALREADY-AUDITED email flow and write as little new provisioning code as possible. Do NOT deploy, do NOT run prisma commands (verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`; stale-client "Property does not exist" errors are noise — fix only real errors; node_modules symlinked; NEVER prisma generate). Commit on the branch; report files changed + a short security note.

PROBLEM: hosting plans advertise "1/10/25 mailboxes included" but nothing provisions them — customers see no way to use their bundled email.

DESIGN (implement exactly this — it's the safe, low-new-code path):
1. Study lib/actions-email-hosting.ts (subscribeEmail ~240, addMailbox ~599, provisionMailboxOnMailcow), the EmailSubscription + Mailbox + EmailPlan models, and lib/mailcow.ts. Note the SECURITY invariant: EmailSubscription dupe-check is GLOBAL (one subscription per domain across ALL users — the 2026-07-25 cross-tenant-takeover fix); external domains stay verified:false until DNS is confirmed; addMailbox already enforces all of this. DO NOT weaken any of it.
2. Seed/upsert **bundled** EmailPlans (free, priceCents:0) with mailboxes 1 / 10 / 25 (matching the hosting Starter/Business/Pro `mailboxes` counts) — a prisma/seed-hosting-email-plans.ts standalone seed (idempotent, like seed-hosting-plans.ts). Mark them so they don't show in the paid Business Email storefront (e.g. active:false or a naming convention the storefront filters — check how EmailPlan list is queried and keep bundled plans OUT of the paid picker).
3. New action `setupHostingEmail(accountId)` in lib/actions-hosting.ts (or a small lib/hosting-email.ts): owner-or-admin + assertNotImpersonating; loads the hosting account + its plan's mailbox count; if the account's primaryDomain has NO existing EmailSubscription (reuse the SAME global dupe check as subscribeEmail — if another user already has it, return the same "contact support" error), create a COMPLIMENTARY EmailSubscription (userId=account owner, domainName=primaryDomain, emailPlanId=the matching bundled plan, external=true, verified=false, status:ACTIVE, no wallet charge, autoRenew tied to the hosting account). Idempotent: if the account already has its bundled subscription, no-op. Record an audit log row.
4. Wire it into the hosting **Email tab** (components/customer/hosting/HostingTabs.tsx — find the "Set up email →" placeholder): show "N mailboxes included with your {plan} plan", a "Set up my email" button calling setupHostingEmail, and once the subscription exists, link to /dashboard/email (the existing Business Email UI that already lists the subscription + addMailbox + shows the DNS records to verify the domain). Do NOT build a parallel mailbox UI — reuse /dashboard/email.
5. Do NOT auto-charge, do NOT write any new Mailcow/SSH code — the actual mailbox creation happens through the existing audited addMailbox path when the customer adds a mailbox in /dashboard/email.

Security note in your report: confirm the global domain-dedup guard is intact and that bundled email cannot be minted for a domain another tenant owns. tsc clean, commit, report.

content.text:
Done. Committed to `feature/hosting-email` as `26293e9`. tsc is clean (no errors).

## What was built

Bundled hosting email that honors the "1/10/25 mailboxes included" promise by reusing the already-audited Business Email flow end to end — minimal new provisioning code, zero new Mailcow/SSH code.

Files changed:
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-email/prisma/seed-hosting-email-plans.ts` (new) — idempotent standalone seed (modeled on `seed-hosting-plans.ts`/`seed-email-plans.ts`) creating 3 bundled `EmailPlan` rows: mailbox counts 1/10/25 mirroring the hosting Starter/Business/Pro `mailboxes`, `priceCents:0`, `active:false`, name suffix "(bundled)".
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-email/lib/hosting-email.ts` (new) — `setupHostingEmail(accountId)` + `getHostingEmailStatus(accountId)` server actions.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-email/components/customer/hosting/EmailTab.tsx` (new) — the Email tab UI.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-email/components/customer/hosting/HostingTabs.tsx` (modified) — registered the new "Email" tab (there was no pre-existing "Set up email →" placeholder; the hosting account detail had no Email tab at all, so I added one between Domains and Apps).

Behavior: the Email tab shows "N mailboxes included with your {plan} plan" + a "Set up my email" button. `setupHostingEmail` creates a complimentary `EmailSubscription` (owner userId, primaryDomain, matching bundled plan, `external:true`, `verified:false`, `status:ACTIVE`, no wallet charge, `expiresAt` tied to the account), writes an audit row (`hostingemail.setup`), and is idempotent. Once the subscription exists the tab links to `/dashboard/email` (the existing UI that lists it, does `addMailbox`, and shows the DNS records) — no parallel mailbox UI.

## Security note

The 2026-07-25 cross-tenant-takeover guard is fully intact and reused, not reimplemented:

- `setupHostingEmail` uses the identical GLOBAL dedup query as `subscribeEmail`/`orderEmailHosting` — `emailSubscription.findFirst({ where: { domainName, status: { not: "CANCELLED" } } })` with no `userId` scope. If another tenant already holds the domain, it mints **nothing** and returns the same "contact support" ownership-verification error. Bundled email cannot be created for a domain another tenant owns.
- If the owner already holds the domain (bundled or paid), it's an idempotent no-op returning the existing subscription.
- The complimentary subscription is created `external:true, verified:false`, so holding the row grants no power over the domain's mail — the existing `addMailbox`/`retryMailboxProvision` DNS-verification gate still blocks any Mailcow write until the customer proves DNS control. No new mailbox/Mailcow code was added, so no new path to the shared instance exists.
- Owner-or-admin check plus `assertNotImpersonating` (support can't mint a grant in a customer's name).
- `getHostingEmailStatus` deliberately scopes its display lookup to the owner's own subscription, so a cross-tenant-held domain simply surfaces the "Set up my email" button, whose action then returns the safe support error — no cross-tenant state is ever revealed.

Bundled plans stay out of the paid picker via `active:false` (the `/dashboard/email` storefront filters `active:true`, and `orderEmailHosting` rejects any non-active plan), belt-and-braces with `priceCents:0`.

Not deployed, no prisma commands run (verified with `npx tsc --noEmit`). Note: the seed still needs to be run against the DB before `setupHostingEmail` can find bundled plans — until then it returns a graceful "contact support" message rather than erroring.
